payload.text: Explain the logic to find the middle node of a linked list in a single pass.
expected_concepts: slow at middle when fast at end
Fast pointer reaches end when slow reaches middle
No need to count nodes first
termination: while(fast && fast->next) gives second middle for even-length lists
invariant: when fast moves 2k steps total, slow has moved k — so slow is always at the midpoint of fast's coverage
common_mistakes: counts nodes first then traverses to n/2 — two passes instead of one
wrong termination condition for even-length lists — returns wrong middle
fast starts at head->next giving different middle for even-length lists
payload.reference_answer: The middle node of a linked list is found using two pointers: a slow pointer moving one step at a time and a fast pointer moving two steps at a time. When fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle.
possible_followups: when fast reaches last node, slow is at middle (for odd length)
when fast becomes null, slow is at second middle (for even length)
choice of termination condition determines which middle for even-length lists
O(n) time single pass — avoids counting nodes then traversing again
O(1) space — no array or extra storage
used as subroutine in merge sort for linked lists
